statement.excerpt: Every member of the government having access to ChatGPT — something that is not even necessarily the case! — does not make this software useful, let alone essential, and if OpenAI burns a bunch of money "making it work for them," it still won't be essential, because Large Language Models are not actually that useful for doing stuff!
statement.document_title: How To Argue With An AI Booster

from_speaker: if OpenAI burns a bunch of money "making it work for them"
Large Language Models are not actually that useful for doing stuff
our_interpretation: The government means the US federal government, following the surrounding examples.

The antecedent requires substantial expenditure by OpenAI on adapting ChatGPT to government work. A contract ceiling, discounted access, or government purchases alone does not establish that expenditure.
Essential means material operational dependence: removing ChatGPT would substantially disrupt an important government service and an ordinary substitute would not readily avoid the disruption.
The general statement about usefulness supplies the forecast's explanation; usefulness alone does not establish essentiality.
criteria.support_condition: After the spending condition is met, operational records showing successful removal or replacement without material service disruption would support the forecast's direction. A finite observation cannot conclusively establish that ChatGPT will never become essential.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After substantial OpenAI customization spending is established, an audit or operational record demonstrates material government-service dependence on ChatGPT, including substantial disruption from withdrawal and difficulty replacing it.
